correspondence.component_scope: Selected southeastern opening and northwest/westward approach to Wild Horse Creek
correspondence.finding: The original covers the complete selected opening and its northwestward course across the Presidio County plain southwest of US90, including all small stored joins and the westward turn toward the separately mapped Wild Horse Creek. Roads, small isolated water symbols and contours are readable, but the source does not depict a continuous watercourse along this selected approach or its complete transfer into Wild Horse Creek. Proximity to the named creek and common plain setting are insufficient to identify these parts as that creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern mapped Wild Horse Creek reach and northwestern bends
correspondence.finding: From the receiving-channel setting after the westward approach, the selected northward and northwestern succession corresponds at ordinary corridor scale to the repeatedly labelled Wild Horse Creek. The original shows its dashed blue course across the Presidio–Jeff Davis county setting, the Miller Ranch Road/A Miller Road surroundings and the incoming Tally Slough network. The short selected joins and bends are within this continuous named channel corridor. Exact bank positions and perennial flow are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Wild Horse Creek past the Chispa Mountain setting into southern Lobo Valley
correspondence.finding: The mapped Wild Horse Creek continues northwest then north along the selected route, through the US90/Chispa Mountain surroundings and the southern Lobo Valley. The source shows the same sequence of valley bends and side drainage entries at ordinary corridor scale, with small nearby closed water symbols distinguished from the creek. Those nearby water bodies are not substituted for selected through-lake connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected Lobo Valley detour through the US90 and Lobo Road field-drain setting
correspondence.finding: The original separately depicts the labelled Wild Horse Creek, road/rail lines, parcel boundaries and rectilinear blue drainage features in the cultivated Lobo Valley. The selected route makes crossings and an eastern detour before returning to the labelled channel. The source does not establish every selected transfer across this road and field-drain setting. A named creek on both sides and nearby blue drainage lines do not prove the missing selected through-links. The observation is not a diagnosis of model or map error.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Lobo Valley, Eagle Flat Draw vicinity, Van Horn and the Interstate10 crossing
correspondence.finding: The selected northward continuation and northeastward bend east of Van Horn correspond to the original mapped Wild Horse Creek. Contiguous cartography covers the northern Lobo Valley, the Eagle Flat Draw vicinity, the constricted valley alongside the Wylie Mountains, the crossing of Interstate10 and the receiving northward course east of town. Each stored intermediate part and join is accounted for at ordinary corridor scale. The separately mapped Hackberry Creek is context, not an asserted alternative name for the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Wild Horse Creek, local small-water and drainage settings, and Wild Horse Draw
correspondence.finding: The original follows the selected northward valley corridor through the Ranch Road2185 surroundings and past the separately depicted Sulphur Creek/rectilinear drainage network to the northern mapped Wild Horse Creek. The creek is shown near several small closed blue water features. The northern original also prints Wild Horse Draw by the upper end of the mapped blue channel. This supports a bounded local creek/draw identification only; it does not establish a formal alias relation, precise passage through every small pond, current managed connections or a creek continuing across the farther northern plain.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northern dryland extension and approach into the Salt Basin playa
correspondence.finding: Beyond the northern mapped creek/draw segment, the selected route continues north, turns west across the plain, crosses the Wingo Road setting and then approaches the southern Salt Basin playa from the southeast. The original covers this full extension, its bends and joins, but does not show a continuous watercourse along the selected cross-plain connection into the playa. The Bull Canyon/Baylor Draw surroundings and Salt Basin label provide geography only. The selected line itself and the endorheic model classification cannot supply the missing natural or managed hydraulic connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Final selected part and actual terminal in the southern Salt Basin playa
correspondence.finding: The actual last stored part and its endpoint lie within the southern large blue-outlined, stippled playa polygon east of State Highway54, in the Salt Basin cartographic setting. The preceding southeast approach and the actual endpoint were inspected together, rather than replacing the terminal with an upstream creek point or a nearby label. This establishes the generalized terminal playa setting. The source does not assign an individual lake name to this polygon or establish present inundation, an exact shoreline, an ordinary river mouth or the unproved upstream-to-playa connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Extreme selected unnamed opening
correspondence.finding: Both acquired watercourse publications depict nearby convergent upper drainage, but the extreme selected northwestern opening and its initial diagonal connection do not have a continuous source line. The later part of the opening reaches the depicted drainage. A nearby line or modeled continuity does not establish the missing initial passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward upper feeder to the Caracarani setting
correspondence.finding: The southeastward course and its receiving bend correspond to a continuous depicted unnamed drainage. The mapped Caracarani branches approach from the east; no Caracarani name is imposed on the entire initial feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southward Caracarani reach and receiving join
correspondence.finding: The selected southward bends follow the mapped Quebrada Caracarani / Q. Caracarani course. Its joins and continuation to the receiving course are visible at ordinary corridor scale. The western incoming branch is distinct from the selected northern feeder. No exact formal name-change vertex is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper receiving course and eastward-to-southward bend
correspondence.finding: The acquired bounded cartography depicts the selected receiving course, its southeastward continuation, broad eastern bend and southwestward exit continuously. The source attribute associated with the receiving main valley is Río Lluta / Rio Lluta. Intermediate stored joins correspond at ordinary regional scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward middle Lluta and westward valley turn
correspondence.finding: The southward canyon sequence and westward valley turn follow a continuous depicted main watercourse. The many short stored parts and their intermediate joins were compared as one selected corridor, without requiring matching source vertices or assigning tributary labels to the mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Chironta approach, reservoir/dam setting and downstream return
correspondence.finding: The watercourse cartography follows the selected main valley through this setting but does not depict a usable current reservoir boundary, dam crossing and chosen downstream transfer. The separately read 2023 inauguration report establishes the completed Chironta reservoir on the Lluta and regulated downstream water-supply context. That prose does not map the selected managed connector. Discovery-only precise location and the unavailable tunnel article are not substantive connector evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower named valley, southern bend and westward coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The main lower valley, the pronounced southern bend, northwestern return and westward approach have continuous source-watercourse correspondence. Both services directly associate the main course with the Lluta name. This completed lower-valley observation excludes the unresolved final coastal part.

correspondence.component_scope: Final selected coast-ending part
correspondence.finding: The early western portion corresponds to the named lower Lluta, but the selected final southward passage departs from the drawn river-mouth course. The independent site-study maps show the Lluta mouth, coastal lagoon belt and Pacific shore at 1:10,000 and schematic scales. They do not show a continuous passage along the complete selected southern ending. Terminal proximity to the wetland is insufficient to close that connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected Ville Platte opening
correspondence.finding: The headward original maps the selected initial eastward reach in the Mattie Lane and Tate Cove Road setting west of Coulee de Manuel. Roads, buildings, open land and separate drainage lines are shown, but no mapped waterway carries this whole selected opening east into the coulee. The selected line meets the mapped coulee corridor farther east near the Nornet Street setting. The larger upper map and detailed original agree on this separation.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Material opening-connection gap. The named coulee nearby does not establish the unsupported initial through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Coulee de Manuel and southwestward receiving bayou corridor
correspondence.finding: The detailed headward map labels Coulee de Manuel and depicts its southward continuation beside Ville Platte and across the highway/railway setting. The upper original carries the selected corridor south and southwest, past the joining western branch and the joining gully and Bayou Marron settings. The mapped waterway continues through these joins; surrounding agricultural ponds and rectilinear drains are not substituted for the selected bayou. The mapped corridor is supported after the unresolved opening, without extending the coulee name over every downstream reach.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported downstream coulee and receiving corridor at ordinary channel/valley scale; local modeled bend shortcuts are not exact-bank claims.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper bayou corridor past Eunice and tributary entries
correspondence.finding: The upper original follows the selected southwestward receiving corridor past the Bayou Marron entry and northwestern Eunice surroundings, across the Highway 190 setting and onward toward the Iota corridor. It depicts the entries of Tigerpoint Gully, Richards Gully and Bayou Berwick along this route. Overlap with the middle original preserves the same receiving corridor across its eastward tributary joins. These side streams remain separately named; no lake-to-lake or cross-field transfer is needed for this supported interval.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported upper receiving corridor and ordinary intermediate joins. The absence of a repeated name label at every upper bend is not treated as a connectivity gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Bayou des Cannes, Iota–Evangeline corridor and Mermentau headward junctions
correspondence.finding: The middle original follows the selected bayou south past Iota and Evangeline and through the Interstate 10 crossing. It explicitly labels Bayou des Cannes on the lower part of this approach, maps its receiving junction with the large eastern bayou corridor, and shows the western Bayou Nezpique branch joining before the channel continues through Mermentau. The eastern incoming channel remains a distinct tributary corridor. These are actual depicted junctions, not basin membership used as a connection.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported Bayou des Cannes approach, principal eastern and western bayou joins, and continuation into the named Mermentau corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Mermentau channel and transition into Lake Arthur
correspondence.finding: The middle and lake originals overlap along the Mermentau channel below the village of Mermentau. They depict its continued meandering course past the Bayou Queue de Tortue entry and into the northeastern end of Lake Arthur. The 10003/10004 fragment boundary falls within this mapped continuous receiving corridor; no unsupported fragment jump is supplied by model continuity.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported named receiving channel, lateral bayou entry, fragment transition and actual Lake Arthur entry.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Arthur through-passage and connection to Grand Lake
correspondence.finding: The lake original names Lake Arthur and depicts the selected route across its open water, through the southern narrows and the Mermentau River channel beside Lowry, and south through the channel/wetland complex to Grand Lake. The selected route crosses the mapped Intracoastal Waterway junction at the northern Grand Lake approach. The map visibly connects the inlet, open-water passage and outgoing channel; the lake name alone is not used as proof of a through-link. Nearby managed drains, Lacassine waters and wetland islands remain distinct.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported through-lake and connecting-channel correspondence, including the Intracoastal Waterway crossing. Current flow direction, lock operation and discharge are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Grand Lake passage and southwestern outlet
correspondence.finding: The overlapping lake and lower originals name Grand Lake and Mermentau River in the open-water corridor. They carry the selected route south through the lake and southwest into the mapped outlet near Catfish Bend. The outlet continues past the Catfish Lake/Locust Bay setting into the lower Mermentau River. The selected route follows the connected open water and receiving outlet; adjacent marshes and side lakes are not assumed to be through-connections.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported Grand Lake inlet-to-outlet passage and lower-river transition at ordinary lake/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Mermentau, navigational channel and Kings Bayou setting
correspondence.finding: The lower original follows the Mermentau channel south past the Little Chenier Bayou and Little Pecan Bayou entries, then west along the Grand Chenier corridor. It labels Mermentau River Navigational Channel and depicts the selected westward channel and southward turn across the Highway 82 setting. The detailed terminal original shows its connection to the broad Kings Bayou waterbody and the separately named Hog Bayou branch. The named and managed channel interval is mapped continuously before the unsupported final coastal-strip passage.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported lower river, navigational-channel corridor and connection into the Kings Bayou waterbody. No assertion about present channel controls or operating condition.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower and detailed terminal originals depict the selected final southward line leaving the Kings Bayou waterbody, crossing the land strip at Hackberry Beach, and continuing to the gulf-side endpoint. They do not depict a waterway across this strip along the selected final connection. Hog Bayou instead continues east from the waterbody, while other mapped outlet routes are geographically different. The actual selected end is retained rather than replaced with a more convenient Mermentau outlet.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Material terminal-connection gap; this is a missing through-waterway across intervening land, not an exact-bank or vertex-alignment requirement.

correspondence.component_scope: western headward opening and eastward approach
correspondence.finding: No inspected original establishes the western opening, its feeder identity, or the first eastward connection.

correspondence.component_scope: southern interior excursion and return
correspondence.finding: The selected path bends south and returns north. No inspected map establishes a continuous channel around this substantial interior excursion or its intervening joins.

correspondence.component_scope: northern interior loop and eastward crossing
correspondence.finding: The long northward continuation, northern turn and eastward crossing remain without source-matched channel or waterbody transfers. A regional delta label would not close these gaps.

correspondence.component_scope: southeastern approach to the fragment transition
correspondence.finding: No inspected original establishes the southeastward corridor into the Breves-area transition or a name applying to this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: join between selected fragments
correspondence.finding: The supplied fragments share an endpoint, but a source-confirmed geographical connection is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: lower southward/eastward continuation and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: Neither the lower selected through-link nor its actual terminal is established by inspected original cartography. Chart4351 catalogue coverage and a nearby Parauaú discovery label are insufficient.

correspondence.component_scope: floodplain, tidal, lake or managed transfers
correspondence.finding: No source confirms or excludes local floodplain, tidal, lake or managed connectors along this selection. The selected geometry alone does not establish hydraulic continuity or a river-name hierarchy.
